# Copilot skills

Copilot skills are markdown runbooks that the Copilot loads on demand. On each turn
the model sees only a one-line catalog entry (name and description) for each skill
available to it. It pulls a skill's full body in when the task calls for it.

These are skills **for the Copilot**. They are not the Mantle skills in a user's
project (`skills/<id>/skill.md`), and not the IDE skills that `rasa tools skills
install` copies into a project (`rasa/cli/tools/skills_data/`).

Skills are parsed by `rasa/builder/copilot/skill_catalog.py`.

## How a run gets its skills

- `COPILOT_SKILL_POLICIES` in `rasa/builder/copilot/pydantic_ai/skills.py` maps the
  project's engine to a `SkillPolicy`: the use cases whose skills the run offers. Only
  Mantle has a policy today, so a CALM project gets no skills.
- Each offered skill becomes a deferred pydantic-ai capability. The model sees one
  catalog line, `- <name>: <description>`, and loads the body with `load_capability`.
- Nothing carries over between user messages: every turn starts with no skill loaded.
- The model reads a loaded skill's `references/*.md` file with
  `load_skill_reference(skill_name, reference_path)`, where `reference_path` is
  `references/<file>.md`. Only files packaged with the skill can be read.

## Layout

```
skills/
  <use_case>/                 # one directory per SkillUseCase value, e.g. mantle/
    <name>/                   # the directory name is the skill name
      SKILL.md
      references/             # optional
        <topic>.md
```

- **Use case.** A use-case directory must be a `SkillUseCase` value in
  `skill_catalog.py`. To add a use case, add the enum value and the directory together.
- **Names.** A skill's name must equal its directory name. Use lowercase letters,
  digits and single hyphens (at most 64 characters). Names must be unique across
  all use cases. Don't prefix them with the use case.
- **References.** Only top-level `references/*.md` files are read; anything else in
  the skill directory is ignored.

## `SKILL.md`

```markdown
---
name: building-skills
description: >-
  Load before creating or editing any file under skills/: skill.md
  instructions, tools.py, and the control ladder.
version: 1.0.0
tools: [read_project_files, update_multiple_files, validate_project]
source:
  path: mantle/mantle-building-skills
  version: 0.2.5
---

# Building Mantle skills

...
```

| Key | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | Equals the directory name. |
| `description` | yes | At most 1024 characters. The model decides whether to load the skill from this text alone, so say when to use it ("Load before ..."). |
| `version` | yes | `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. Bump it on every content change: patch for wording, minor for new guidance, major for a changed workflow. |
| `tools` | no | Exactly the Copilot tools the body and its references name. Each must be offered to the use case's runs. |
| `source` | no | The IDE skill this one was adapted from. `path` is relative to `rasa/cli/tools/skills_data/`; `version` is that skill's `metadata.version` this copy matches. |

Any other key is rejected, and the skill is skipped.

## Writing the body

1. Name Copilot tools exactly, in backticks, and list every one of them in `tools:`.
   Don't name a tool the Copilot is not offered (for example `train_rasa_assistant`);
   say what the user should do instead.
2. No shell commands or CLI invocations (`rasa train`, `grep ...`). No paths outside
   the user's project (such as `.rasa/docs/`). No IDE setup (`.mcp.json`, restarting
   a session). The Copilot has none of these.
3. No documentation-site URLs. The Copilot may only cite URLs that come from its own
   search results, so name the docs page instead.
4. Don't restate rules the Copilot system prompt already applies to every turn (the
   tool budget, citations, tone, validating before reporting success). A skill holds
   only what is specific to its task.
5. To override a global rule on purpose, or to correct a fact the system prompt has
   out of date, put it in a `## Overrides` section. For that task it takes
   precedence over the system prompt.
6. To point to another skill, write ``load the `<name>` skill`` with its exact name.
   Never name the IDE skill it was adapted from.
7. Move long tables and examples into `references/` and say in the body when to read
   each one, naming its path (`references/<file>.md`) so the model can pass it to
   `load_skill_reference`.
8. Keep the body under 16,000 characters (about 4k tokens); references don't count.
9. When you talk about the user's Mantle skills, write "Mantle skill" or
   `skills/<id>/skill.md`. In the Copilot prompt the word "skill" means both.

`tests/builder/copilot/test_skill_catalog.py` checks the packaged skills against
these rules (rules 1, 2, 3, 6, and 8), the frontmatter, and `source` drift.

## Skills adapted from IDE skills

When a skill is adapted from an IDE skill under `rasa/cli/tools/skills_data/`, set
`source` to the IDE skill and the version it matches. When the IDE skill changes,
port the change and bump both `version` and `source.version`.
